First, we rewrite the limit as

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2x-3}.
$$

The numerator here is a bounded, oscillating function with

$$
|-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x|\le 5.
$$

However, the denominator $2x-3$ grows without bound as $x\to \infty .$ So the denominator is growing much faster than the numerator, and we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2x-3}=0.
$$

We can see this from the graph of $y=\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x},$ shown below:
